environment.frontend: vidra-user production build served as `node .next/standalone/server.js` on 3111 behind a pipe-only proxy on 3110 that routes /api/v1, /healthz, /readyz, /metrics and /.well-known to core - ONE origin, because vidra_refresh is SameSite=Lax and Path=/api/v1/auth. The proxy drops the client's Accept-Encoding. Node 26.8.1.
environment.clamav: REAL ClamAV 1.5.4 (brew), its own clamd.conf, freshclam database signature set 28117 (daily 355647 + main 3287027 + bytecode 80 signatures), TCP 127.0.0.1:3310, LogClean yes. CLAMAV_ADDR=127.0.0.1:3310, CLAMAV_TIMEOUT=60s.
environment.whisper: REAL whisper.cpp 1.9.2 whisper-server on 127.0.0.1:8099 with the MULTILINGUAL ggml-tiny.bin (74 MiB), default --inference-path /inference, 4 threads, Metal backend. WHISPER_ENABLED=true, WHISPER_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:8099, WHISPER_DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=en. Run under a supervisor because whisper.cpp aborts on an unknown language tag.
environment.fixture_origin: a local Python HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:8199 serving a benign ffmpeg-made mp4 and the EICAR body as video/mp4, for the URL-import lane.
environment.stall_endpoint: a local Python server on 127.0.0.1:8098 that accepts the multipart POST to /inference and never answers, for the timeout lane.
environment.media_fixtures: two clips with REAL speech: macOS `say` -> aiff -> ffmpeg mp4 (9.19 s and 7 s, h264 + aac). EICAR fixtures are assembled from two string fragments at runtime and are committed nowhere.
environment.external_dependency: none at run time. The only network use was fetching ggml-tiny.bin from huggingface.co and the ClamAV database from database.clamav.net before the lab started.
environment.toolchain: Go 1.26.2, ffmpeg 8.1, Node 26.8.1, 14 GiB free disk.

whisper_contract.shape: multipart/form-data POST to <WHISPER_ENDPOINT>/inference with file (16 kHz mono s16le WAV extracted by ffmpeg -vn -ac 1 -ar 16000 -c:a pcm_s16le), response_format=verbose_json, temperature=0, optional language; response segments[] of {start,end,text} in seconds rendered to WebVTT.
whisper_contract.confirmed_against: whisper.cpp 1.9.2 whisper-server answered exactly that shape; the client also ignores the response's own `language` field, so a transcript is stored under whatever tag the creator asked for.
whisper_contract.trigger: POST /api/v1/videos/{id}/captions/auto (202) + GET on the same path for status; drain loop is worker-role only and starts on captionjob.BootCapable(), never on the runtime toggle.
whisper_contract.timeout_knob: NONE - defaultWhisperTimeout in internal/media/whisper.go is a compile-time 10 minutes (measured: claimed 07:25:00, failed 07:35:00).
whisper_contract.retry: internal/captionjob: baseBackoff 1 min doubling, capped at 1 h, dead-letter at 5 attempts. Measured +1 min then +2 min naturally.

sc5_fail_policy.mode_knob: MALWARE_SCAN_MODE, default fail-closed. It decides ONLY what happens when the scan cannot complete; an INFECTED verdict fails in every mode.
sc5_fail_policy.fail_closed: clamd stopped -> upload AND URL import both failed; audit 'outcome=scan_error policy=fail-closed'
sc5_fail_policy.quarantine: -> quarantined, visible in the admin quarantine queue; audit 'policy=quarantine'
sc5_fail_policy.fail_open: -> PUBLISHED UNSCANNED with NO audit row - only a WARN log line 'malware scan failed; publishing anyway (MALWARE_SCAN_MODE=fail-open)'
sc5_fail_policy.unset_clamav_addr: means scanning is off (config forbids the alternative). A real mp4 with EICAR appended uploaded and PUBLISHED publicly, unscanned, with no boot warning and no log line. The only honest surface is /admin/infrastructure's malware_scan row: enabled false, configured false, with prose saying files publish unscanned. INT-04 requires scanning to gate ALL ingestion; the shipped default gates none.
sc5_fail_policy.admin_system_before: clamd stopped mid-run: status 'ok', nine healthy components (postgres, redis, s3, storage, smtp, search, ffmpeg, mfa_kek, settings_sync), NO scanner component at all; /admin/infrastructure still said malware_scan enabled:true configured:true because that row is static config.
sc5_fail_policy.admin_system_after: clamd up -> clamav ok, instance ok. clamd down -> clamav down, instance DEGRADED, sentence 'the malware scanner is unreachable and MALWARE_SCAN_MODE=fail-closed, so every upload and every URL import is failing: clamav: dial: dial tcp the configured address: connect: connection refused'; under fail-open the same failure reads '...is being published WITHOUT being scanned'.
sc5_fail_policy.defect_in_the_fix: the first cut passed net.Dialer's error through verbatim, putting CLAMAV_ADDR on an admin page - the exact value admin_infra_test forbids there by name. Caught by running the probe against the live lab, not its unit tests. Address and bare host are now redacted; grep -c '3310' over the whole response body is 0; a test pins it.

findings_needing_a_ruling: A malware rejection is invisible to the creator: upload session settles state=completed failure_reason='', import job settles state=done with no error, Studio shows a bare FAILED badge - beside a quarantined video that gets a full explanatory sentence. Not patched: the wording is a product decision.
MALWARE_SCAN_MODE=fail-open publishing unscanned media leaves no audit row at all, only a WARN log line.

caption_generate rows in job_runs carry empty correlation_id, request_id and actor_id on 4 of 4 rows, where upload_finalize and video_transcode are stamped on 2 of 2. internal/captionjob never calls jobtrace; uploadfinalize is the pattern to copy. A17's 'six projected queues do not call the job recorder' is half right: the row exists (migration 0083's trigger), the identity does not.
The Whisper round-trip timeout is a compile-time 10 minutes with no knob.

A well-formed unknown language tag (zz) passes Vidra's BCP-47-ish validator and ABORTS whisper.cpp, so any creator can kill a shared transcription service. Vidra has no supported-language set to validate against.
One click on Studio's 'Generate automatically' silently replaced a creator's hand-written en track - label, bytes and all - with 'Auto-generated'. No warning, no undo. Verified in Chromium.
UpsertCaption keeps the original created_at and there is no updated_at, so nothing distinguishes an edited caption from an untouched one.
EICAR is a whole-file signature: a real mp4 with EICAR appended scans clean on clamd 1.5.4 (verified with clamdscan). This lane proves the gate and the plumbing, not clamd's detection depth.
